args.text: When the description explicitly states multiple actions in sequence, model each action as an activity and connect them in the described order, including actions that occur after a decision or optional branch.

trace.reason: Check documented guidance for representing explicitly described activities and their order.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.

args.text: When the description states that an activity may occur as an optional alternative, model the activity and its branch before continuing to the subsequent selection or decision.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers optional activities and their branches.

result.rule: When the description says that one of several alternatives is selected, or that an activity may occur: Model the choice or optional activity with an appropriate gateway, and reconnect the resulting paths before subsequent common work.

When the description makes an activity contingent on whether a stated condition holds: Model the condition with an exclusive gateway at the point where it affects the flow, and route the contingent activity only along the branch where the condition holds. Do not invent an outcome for the other branch.

When the description states an activity and separately specifies criteria used to perform it: Label the activity with its concise core action; do not add the criteria to the activity label unless they are needed to distinguish it from another activity.

When the description names multiple required activities in a phase, gives no order among them, and states that a later outcome occurs only after the phase is finished: Model each activity separately, use a parallel split for the unordered activities, and join their branches before modeling the later outcome.

args.text: When the description says an activity may occur before a later common decision or action, model the activity on an optional branch and reconnect that branch with the other path before the common work.

args.text: When a process description states its start and end conditions and describes activities, model elements with concise labels that faithfully reflect those described events and actions; avoid generic event labels and paraphrases that change the described activity.

trace.reason: Check existing documented guidance on faithful BPMN element labels before proposing a general labeling guideline.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

args.text: When a process description states its start and end conditions and describes activities, model elements with concise labels that faithfully reflect those described events and actions; avoid generic event labels and paraphrases that change the described activity.

result.rule: When the description names an activity or milestone for which a BPMN task is being labeled: Label the task to preserve the action and purpose stated in the description; do not substitute a related but different action or milestone.

When the description states an activity and separately specifies criteria used to perform it: Label the activity with its concise core action; do not add the criteria to the activity label unless they are needed to distinguish it from another activity.

When the description establishes an overarching subject or context that applies to several separately stated activities: Label each task with its stated action and purpose, omitting repeated context and qualifiers unless needed to distinguish the activity; do not add unsupported details.

When the description states that an actor identifies or determines a need before subsequent work begins: Model the identification as a task after a start event; do not represent the stated action only as the start event.

args.text: When the description states an event trigger or outcome, or names an activity: Label the corresponding BPMN event or activity with a concise, faithful description of that trigger, outcome, or action; do not use generic event labels or alter the stated action.
